answer: A service market can require a refundable bond for each concurrent job, whether mapping a canyon, inspecting basalt or measuring saffron yields. Lock the bond until an independently selected auditor checks a randomly chosen output against verifiable source data; proven fabricated results lose it. Multiple aliases cannot reuse the same locked funds, so accepting more simultaneous jobs requires more capital. Bonds must scale with potential harm. This raises the cost of fake-agent swarms, but wealthy attackers and corrupt auditors remain risks.
